clue.text: Investigates tense gangster finding religious office

parts.note: pries means pokes about or investigates

hood is slang for a hoodlum or gangster

explanation.surface: A detective probing a nervous mobster stumbles on a church post.
explanation.definitionFit: The office or rank of a cleric, a religious post, is the standing of a priest.

clue.text: Rather small-minded about the centre of Perth

indicators.note: one piece placed about another surrounds it

parts.note: petty means small-minded

indicators.note: the centre of points to the middle letter of the word Perth

explanation.surface: A rather narrow-minded view of the heart of a Scottish city.
explanation.definitionFit: Pretty can mean fairly or quite, as in 'pretty good'.

clue.text: Descriptive line from Boris, upset about article?

upset means the letters of Boris are knocked over into a new order

parts.note: A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A line from Boris Johnson, rattled over a newspaper piece.
explanation.definitionFit: On a weather map this contour joins points of equal pressure, describing the weather.

clue.text: Expensive case of lemonade drinks for jumpers

parts.note: steep means expensive

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outside letters, first and last

parts.note: chasers are drinks taken after another, such as a beer after a spirit

explanation.surface: A pricey crate of soft drinks for knitwear, it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumpers' looks like sweaters; it means racehorses that jump fences.
explanation.definitionFit: Horses in races over fences are jumpers.

clue.text: Capital rugby player, a buffoon!

definitions.meaning: A London rugby union club, so a player for the capital's team
a clown or comic fool, the stock character of pantomime

explanation.surface: Calling a London rugby player a clown.
explanation.definitionFit: The diamond-suited clown of Italian comedy gave his name to a London rugby club.

clue.text: Comes a cropper holding up killers

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read bottom to top
holding means the phrase keeps the letters inside its words

explanation.surface: Someone falls flat while holding back murderers.
explanation.definitionFit: These black and white whales are named killer whales.

clue.text: Emperor penguins ultimately eaten by sailor

indicators.note: one piece being eaten by another means it sits inside it

parts.note: a tar is an old word for a sailor

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word penguins

explanation.surface: Emperor penguins, the birds, end up as a seaman's dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Emperor penguins' reads as one bird species, but 'Emperor' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A Russian emperor bore this title before the revolution.

clue.text: Key frame?

definitions.meaning: a frame is the bones of a body or a bare structure

explanation.surface: A query about a key picture in a film.
explanation.definitionFit: A master key filed to open many locks shares its name with the bony framework of a body.

clue.text: Criminal hustlers showing no pity

indicators.note: criminal suggests something bent, so the letters of hustlers are twisted

explanation.surface: Crooked hustlers who are merciless.
explanation.definitionFit: A pitiless, merciless person shows no compassion.

clue.text: Brass-rubbers may be so described as artists

definitions.meaning: people taking rubbings of church brasses make prints, or impressions, of them
painters of the movement of Monet and Renoir

explanation.surface: Church brass-rubbers might pass as painters.
explanation.definitionFit: Monet and Renoir's movement shares its name with those who take prints of brasses.

clue.text: Recall almost always covering fine

indicators.note: one word covering another wraps around it
almost means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: ever means always, as in 'ever hopeful'
OK means fine or all right

explanation.surface: Remembering something that seems forever to have been fine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covering' means the shortened word for always wraps around the word for fine.
explanation.definitionFit: To evoke a memory or era is to bring it back to mind, to call it up.

clue.text: Strange about European Community penchant for lying

indicators.note: one piece sitting about another surrounds it

parts.note: rum is British slang for strange or odd
a bent is a natural inclination or penchant

explanation.surface: An odd fondness for telling fibs, perhaps about Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lying' tempts as untruthfulness; here it means lying down.
explanation.definitionFit: Recumbent describes someone lying down, reclining, as on a recumbent bicycle.

clue.text: Walk to find answer during journeys east

indicators.note: a piece placed during another sits within it

parts.note: trips are journeys
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: A traveller heading east on foot, searching for an answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To traipse is to walk wearily or trudge about.

clue.text: Bizarre and stupid quarrels with no origin

indicators.note: stupid suggests the letters are muddled and senseless, so rearranged
no origin means the word loses its first letter

explanation.surface: Pointless rows can seem odd and silly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no origin' drops the Q of quarrels; 'stupid' rearranges UARRELS.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dreamlike and strangely unreal, like a Dali painting, is bizarre.

clue.text: Engineers search new posts for public transport facilities

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers of the British Army
a quest is a search

indicators.note: new signals the word posts is made into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Engineers look for fresh sites for bus shelters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges POSTS into STOPS. A request stop is a British bus stop where the bus halts only if hailed.
explanation.definitionFit: Places where a bus pulls in only when a passenger signals are features of the bus network.

clue.text: Fake copy finally found in battered tin chest

indicators.note: a piece found in another sits inside it
battered means the letters of tin chest are knocked about
finally points to the last letter of the word copy

explanation.surface: A forged copy turns up in a dented metal trunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Something artificial or man-made rather than genuine is fake.

clue.text: Robs drink, depressed by criticism

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece depressed by another sits below it

parts.note: stick is informal for criticism, as in 'taking stick'

explanation.surface: Someone drinks to drown sorrows after harsh words.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold up a person or bank at gunpoint is to rob them.

clue.text: Line crossed by Aussie mates is absolute nonsense

indicators.note: being crossed by a line means it cuts through, sitting inside

parts.note: cobbers is Australian slang for friends

explanation.surface: Australians drawing a line through something they think is rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: This British slang word means rubbish or nonsense, from rhyming slang.

clue.text: Fiercely sound horn, confronting worker with arrest

parts.note: to toot is to sound a horn
a hand is a manual worker, as in farmhand
to nail is slang for catching or arresting

explanation.surface: A driver honks loudly before a labourer is taken into custody.
explanation.definitionFit: Fighting with this idiom means fighting with all one's might, ferociously.

clue.text: Unusually impulsive VIP missing breakfast?

indicators.note: unusually signals the letters are set out in an unusual order
missing means the letters of VIP are removed from the mix

explanation.surface: An impulsive celebrity skips the morning meal.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove V, I and P from IMPULSIVE and rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A cereal of oats, nuts and dried fruit is a breakfast food; the question mark flags an example.

clue.text: Book one's first-class — that's a surprise

parts.note: one is I as a Roman numeral, with the S of 's

clue.text: Artists young reporters will entertain first

parts.note: cubs are cub reporters, young journalists

clue.text: So far yet not moving

definitions.meaning: up to now, even now, as in 'it is raining even now'

explanation.surface: Progress so far, yet nothing is happening.
explanation.definitionFit: The same word means up to now and also motionless.

clue.text: Obsessions of German chap holding dog back?

parts.note: a pug is a small flat-faced dog

clue.text: Small fruit with fresh flavour

mint means fresh, as in mint condition

explanation.surface: A little fruit with a zingy taste.

clue.text: South American chain oddly missing this dish

clue.text: Shops starting to employ attention-seeker

indicators.note: to employ is to take in, so the words hold the letters within them

explanation.surface: Shops beginning to hire someone desperate to be noticed.
explanation.definitionFit: This whisper is a sound used to catch someone's attention discreetly.

clue.text: Person whose work may be forged

definitions.text: Person whose work may be forged

parts.words: Person whose work may be forged
parts.note: forged suggests faked art, but here it means hammered into shape at a forge
